paragraphs.title: Love of God and Prayer in Distress

answers: Because the LORD hath heard his voice and supplications
Because all men are liars
Because he lives in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “I love the LORD, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications.”
easy.q: Why does the psalmist love the LORD?

answers: He led him to Jerusalem
He inclined His ear unto him
He commanded him to offer a sacrifice
easy.explanation: The psalmist says that the LORD “hath inclined his ear” unto him.
easy.q: What did the LORD do for the psalmist?

answers: Give him riches
Lead him into the land of the living
Deliver his soul
easy.explanation: He cries, “O LORD, I beseech thee, deliver my soul.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers: The sorrows of death and the pains of hell
His desire to fulfill a vow
His joy in the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: Death, the pains of hell, trouble, and sorrow surrounded him, so he called upon the LORD.
medium.q: What caused the psalmist to call upon the name of the LORD?

answers: The courts of the LORD’s house
Severe distress and danger associated with death
The land of the living
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the extreme trouble and danger that seized the psalmist.
medium.q: What does the phrase “the pains of hell” describe in this passage?

answers: The psalmist was delivered, then fell into trouble, and finally prayed
The psalmist faced trouble, called upon the LORD, and asked for deliverance
The psalmist offered a sacrifice, paid a vow, and then faced trouble
medium.explanation: The passage first describes distress, then the psalmist’s cry to the LORD for help.
medium.q: What is the order of events in these verses?

answers: The LORD’s listening causes the psalmist to love Him
The LORD’s listening causes the psalmist to turn away
There is no connection between the two
challenge.explanation: The psalmist begins by expressing love and explains that the LORD has heard his prayer.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the LORD hearing the psalmist and the psalmist loving Him?

answers: The psalmist moves from describing distress to urgently asking for help
The psalmist moves from joy to public thanksgiving
The psalmist moves from rest to fulfilling a vow
challenge.explanation: After describing death, trouble, and sorrow, he calls upon the LORD for deliverance.
challenge.q: What change occurs between verse 3 and verse 4?

answers: It is a direct and urgent appeal to the LORD
It is a story about other people
It is merely a description of a place
challenge.explanation: The psalmist directly calls upon the LORD and asks Him to deliver his soul.
challenge.q: What does the repeated use of the LORD’s name in verse 4 show about the prayer?

paragraphs.title: God’s Compassion and Deliverance from Danger

answers: Gracious, righteous, and merciful
Weak and sorrowful
Unwilling to hear
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 5?

answers: The kings of the earth
The simple
Only the people of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The psalmist declares, “The LORD preserveth the simple.”

answers: Unto its rest
Unto the pains of hell
Unto the place of sorrow
easy.explanation: He says, “Return unto thy rest, O my soul.”
easy.q: Where does the psalmist ask his soul to return?

answers: From death, tears, and falling
From hunger, war, and exile
From thirst, loneliness, and poverty
medium.explanation: The LORD delivered his soul from death, his eyes from tears, and his feet from falling.
medium.q: From what did the LORD deliver the psalmist’s soul?

answers: Those who are inexperienced or vulnerable
Those who offer thanksgiving sacrifices
Those who dwell in the courts of the LORD
medium.explanation: The simple are those who lack experience or strength, whom the LORD preserves.
medium.q: What does “the simple” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD’s deliverance from danger
The promise of another man
His location in the land of the living alone
medium.explanation: Because the LORD dealt bountifully with him and delivered him, he can return to rest.
medium.q: What enables the psalmist to return to rest?

answers: He moves from danger and sorrow to rest and walking before the LORD
He moves from rest to danger and death
He moves from public thanksgiving to loneliness
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from being brought low to receiving help, rest, deliverance, and continued life.
challenge.q: What change does the psalmist experience in verses 6–9?

answers: The LORD’s preservation is shown by His helping the weak and vulnerable
The LORD preserves him by hiding him from everyone
The LORD preserves him by keeping him from prayer
challenge.explanation: The LORD preserves the simple, and the psalmist describes receiving that preserving help.
challenge.q: How are the LORD’s preservation and the psalmist’s deliverance related?

answers: Deliverance from stumbling or collapse
Arrival in the courts of the LORD’s house
Lifting the cup of salvation
challenge.explanation: The phrase pictures the LORD rescuing the psalmist from stumbling and ruin.
challenge.q: What does “my feet from falling” mean in the context of the psalm?

answers: He spoke
He offered a sacrifice
He went to Jerusalem
easy.explanation: He says, “I believed, therefore have I spoken.”
easy.q: What did the psalmist do when he believed?

answers: All men are liars
The LORD is unrighteous
There is no need to pray
easy.explanation: Verse 11 records his words: “All men are liars.”
easy.q: What did the psalmist say in his haste?

answers: What shall I render unto the LORD?
Who will lead me into the land of the living?
When will my tears end?
easy.explanation: He asks, “What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask after describing God’s benefits?

answers: In his haste, his affliction led him to say that all men are liars
His affliction led him to praise every person
His affliction caused him to forget the LORD
medium.explanation: The statement appears directly after, “I was greatly afflicted,” and was spoken in haste.
medium.q: What is the connection between the psalmist’s affliction and his statement about men?

answers: The blessings and good things the LORD has given
The troubles that surrounded the psalmist
The vows of all the people
medium.explanation: The benefits are the many blessings and acts of kindness the LORD has shown him.

answers: The psalmist moves from a distressed statement to grateful reflection
The psalmist moves from deliverance to describing death
The psalmist moves from private prayer to addressing all the people
medium.explanation: After speaking in haste during affliction, he considers the LORD’s benefits and asks how to respond.
medium.q: What change occurs between verses 11 and 12?

answers: The psalmist feels he should respond with gratitude
The psalmist complains that the LORD did not help him
The psalmist wants to flee from the land of the living
challenge.explanation: The question arises from his recognition of the LORD’s many benefits.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the question, “What shall I render unto the LORD?”

answers: He trusts in the LORD while expressing distrust of people during distress
He stops trusting the LORD and trusts only people
He believes people are more faithful than the LORD
challenge.explanation: He declares his belief, yet also reports a severe statement made during affliction.
challenge.q: How can the psalmist’s faith and his statement about men be understood together?

answers: Faith during suffering followed by gratitude for the LORD’s benefits
Jerusalem, sacrifice, and the fulfillment of vows
Preservation of the simple, rest, and walking in the land of the living
challenge.explanation: These verses join faith and suffering with the psalmist’s grateful question about responding to God.

paragraphs.title: Public Thanksgiving and Fulfillment of Vows

answers: The cup of salvation
The pains of hell
His eyes from tears
easy.explanation: He says, “I will take the cup of salvation.”

answers: Pay them unto the LORD
Forget them
Give them to another man
easy.explanation: The psalmist repeatedly says, “I will pay my vows unto the LORD.”
easy.q: What will the psalmist do with his vows?

answers: In the courts of the LORD’s house and in Jerusalem
Among the pains of hell
Only in the land of the living
easy.explanation: The final verse mentions the courts of the LORD’s house and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where will the psalmist praise the LORD at the end of the psalm?

answers: The cup of salvation, a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and fulfilled vows
Escape, weeping, and concealment
The simple, tears, and falling
medium.explanation: The passage includes taking the cup of salvation, offering thanksgiving, and paying vows.
medium.q: What does the psalmist’s thanksgiving include?

answers: An offering expressing gratitude
A prayer made only during danger
A vow that is never fulfilled
medium.explanation: It is an offering made as an expression of thanks to the LORD.

answers: To the LORD, in the presence of all His people
To one man, in secret
To the simple, in the land of the living
medium.explanation: He will pay his vows unto the LORD in the presence of all the people.
medium.q: To whom and in what manner will the psalmist pay his vows?

answers: That fulfilling the vow is central to the psalmist’s thanksgiving
That the psalmist is uncertain whether to fulfill the vow
That the vow concerns death but not thanksgiving
challenge.explanation: The repeated promise emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the vow publicly.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of paying vows in verses 14 and 18 emphasize?

answers: The psalmist pays his vows before all the people in the LORD’s house
The psalmist keeps his thanksgiving only in his heart
The psalmist speaks only to the simple
challenge.explanation: He pays his vows in the presence of all the people and in the courts of the LORD’s house.
challenge.q: How does the thanksgiving become public?

answers: Deliverance leads him to thanksgiving, fulfilled vows, and praise
Deliverance causes him to turn away from the LORD’s house
Deliverance prevents him from speaking before the people
challenge.explanation: After deliverance, he takes the cup of salvation, offers thanksgiving, pays his vows, and praises the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the psalmist’s deliverance and his praise?
